citation.title: A Multi-Grid, Single-Mesh Online Learning Framework for Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization Based on Isogeometric Formulation
citation.version_coded: publisher version of record, full-text HTML

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The online Fourier neural operator approach cuts full isogeometric analyses from 210 to 150 and reduces total runtime by roughly one fifth while attaining comparable stress-constrained designs.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 5.2.4 explicitly reports 1.23 for Table 1; first Table 1 case gives 2540.44 s / 2062.78 s = 1.2315 [derived].
claim.alternatives: Table 1 second case gives 2429.20 s versus 2058.63 s; Section 5.2.4/Table 5 report up to 1.78x on the larger grid.

baseline.classical_method: Standard stress-constrained topology optimization with isogeometric analysis, NURBS densities and MMA (Sections 3, 5.1)
baseline.hardware_classical: Windows 10 Pro, i7-11700 CPU, 16 GB RAM (Section 5, numerical setup); division of CPU/GPU work per method not explicit
baseline.hardware_ml: Same system with NVIDIA 3060 GPU, 12 GB GPU RAM; online learning in Python 3.8/PyTorch 1.10.2 (Section 5, numerical setup)
baseline.problem_size: 103 x 52 control points in primary L-bracket cases (Section 5.1); also 63 x 48 and 207 x 102 (Section 5.2.4)
baseline.classical_iterations: 210 iterations or average design-variable change below 1e-?; extracted HTML exponent illegible (Section 5.1)
baseline.classical_time: 2540.44 s first L-bracket; 2429.20 s second L-bracket (Table 1)
baseline.ml_time: 2062.78 s first L-bracket; 2058.63 s second L-bracket (Table 1)
baseline.training_time: 150 epochs per online training/tuning cycle; wall time not separately stated (Section 5.1)
baseline.data_generation_cost: Online examples collected from earlier TO iterations starting after iteration 20; separate generation time not stated (Sections 4, 5.1)
baseline.quality_metric: Final volume fraction and maximum von Mises stress of returned designs (Tables 1-2)
baseline.quality_gap: First L-bracket: volume fraction 0.1489 ML vs 0.1500 classical; maximum stress 24.9176 ML vs 25.2465 classical, with nominal 25 Pa limit (Table 1; Section 5 setup).

R1.evidence: Section 5.1 and Table 1: runtime is compared at the same problem size with similar final volume fractions and stresses, but no reported design-quality error tolerance or matched-quality procedure; the classical first-case stress slightly exceeds the nominal limit.

R2.evidence: Section 5 numerical setup: MATLAB IGA and PyTorch online learning share a stated CPU/GPU machine; the article does not explain which hardware runs each portion or justify the hardware choice. No R2(a)-(e) threshold is established.

R3.evidence: Sections 4 and 5.1: FNO is trained online from preceding optimization iterations for the same problem; there is no offline pretrained dataset.

R4.evidence: Section 5.1 and Tables 1-2: final designs are evaluated by IGA for volume fraction and maximum von Mises stress, but failure or infeasibility rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 2 L-bracket load positions plus 1 quarter-annulus domain (Section 5 setup; Tables 1-2); 2 more resolution cases (Section 5.2.4)

notes: The online method mixes IGA updates and FNO sensitivity predictions. Publisher tables are raster images in the HTML and were read directly. Data availability statement offers data on request; no code link found.
